tess: quick heads-up — ran a focused sweep on L40s comparing fused-paged vs paged-flash variants with KV cache ON. I hit a weird latency floor + microburst at seq=2048, batch=4. Numbers below (all measured on same box, warm kv cache unless noted).

```
# fused-paged (v2-opt)
seq=512 bsz=8 p50=12ms p95=28ms p99=45ms
seq=1024 bsz=4 p50=18ms p95=60ms p99=130ms
seq=2048 bsz=4 p50=40ms p95=115ms p99=290ms  <-- microburst

# paged-flash (v1)
seq=512 bsz=8 p50=14ms p95=32ms p99=55ms
seq=1024 bsz=4 p50=20ms p95=70ms p99=150ms
seq=2048 bsz=4 p50=38ms p95=90ms p99=200ms
```

Observed: fused-paged p95 at 2048 jumps above paged-flash and p99 variance spikes. Flamegraphs show a hot path in the tiling/evictor boundary during KV cache refresh. Posting repro command and profile tarball in the thread.

kevin: interesting — is this only with KV warm? can you repro with a cold KV (full evict) and with prefix cache disabled?

maria: also check if the kernel-selector is choosing the new fused kernel or falling back mid-request. We had a selector change last week (commit 9f3b2a7) that tweaked seq thresholds.

perf-bot: perf-summary (2751239876): fused-paged p95 delta +28ms vs baseline @seq=2048 bsz=4; CPU interrupts spiked during spill. See /artifacts/2751239876/summary.json

sam: quick try — flip the prefetch flag off and rerun 10 iters: `./run_bench --model t5-small --seq 2048 --bs 4 --iters 10 --kv true --prefetch false` — that isolated a similar hump for me a week ago.

ranjit: if flamegraph points to tiling <-> evictor handoff, could be a race in the async prefetch completion handler. Suggest bisect between commit range `main~25..main~10` (around the selector change) and run the same 10-iter suite. If it reproduces, we can revert the selector tweak or tighten the fallback condition.

kevin: +1 on bisect. Also add a short-run with `KV_PREFETCH=0` env var to confirm. Can you attach the nvprof/nsight sample?

```
# repro command tess used
KV_PREFETCH=1 ./bench --gpu L40s --model gpt-small --seq 2048 --bs 4 --iters 50 --kv true --save-profile=2751239876.prof
```

tess: uploaded `2751239876.prof` and a condensed flamegraph (link). Quick findings: 1) fused kernel spends ~30% more time in page-table walk path when a spill occurs; 2) eviction waterfall aligns with p99 spikes. Repro is stable on 3 different L40s boxes.

maria: could this be interaction with the new continuous-batching heuristics? at seq 2048 continuous batching opens a different hotpath for kv linearization.

sam: I'll schedule a 1hr canary on dedicated pool with both kernels toggled and routing policy forcing fused then forcing paged-flash, to see customer impact. Will post results.

ranjit: plan: (1) bisect selector commits, (2) run cold/warm KV matrix with prefetch toggles, (3) collect nsight sample + kernel timelines, (4) temporary routing fallback policy if fused_paged p95 > paged-flash p95 by >20ms.

kevin: tagging @infra-oncall in case we need to yank canary quick. Also leaving a TODO: add a perf regression alert for seq>=1024 bsz<=4 KV=true path.

perf-bot: noted. Creating alert rule `kernelselector.seq-high-latency` and scheduling nightly reruns for 2048x4.

`tess`: thanks — I'll start the bisect now and post results in this thread. If anyone wants access to the perf VMs or the profile tarball, ping me. :mag_right:
